name: 9317 BXI G
notes: FAULHABER's integrated robotics drive: a 21-pole-pair iron-core internal rotor, a low-backlash planetary gearhead (2 stages in 1, needle bearings) and a 15-bit SSI absolute encoder in one 100 x 34 mm housing, L/D 0.34. THREE CAVEATS, all material. (1) NO ONBOARD DRIVER. Unlike every other row in this population the BXI ships without control electronics and is paired with an external FAULHABER MC5010 motion controller, so 987 g is not the same quantity the rest of the catalogue reports. (2) THE PUBLISHED NUMBERS ARE AT DIFFERENT VOLTAGES. Max. torque 20 N.m, max. power output 270 W and max. phase current 13 A are all "up to" figures over a 0-50 V motor range, while the 114 min-1 no-load speed is explicitly stated at 24 V. The 114 min-1 is recorded because it is the only speed FAULHABER publishes, but it is a HALF-VOLTAGE number and the row is therefore speed-pessimistic: against the fitted speed trend it lands at 0.47x predicted for a 10.5:1 reduction, and scaling it to the 50 V ceiling puts it within 1% of the trend. (3) Consequently the tau*w/4 envelope mixes voltages and returns 60 W against the 270 W FAULHABER publishes as mechanical output — a 4.5x gap, where the one other published-power row in the catalogue (MIT Mini Cheetah U8) differs from its envelope by 1.47x. P_peak_W is left null so the row stays on the envelope rule; flip it to 270 only together with a 50 V speed. Against the fitted mass trend the part is 1.88x heavy for its torque, which is what a 10.5:1 iron-core unit should look like next to a population of 30-60:1 modules. OD is the 100 mm on the brochure drawing; a second dimension, 106 mm -0.1, also appears there and is not identified. Ident-no. 000.9001.02.

name: eRob70F-50
notes: SHD 14-50 strain wave gear.
